messages.content: "Can you provide me with the exhibition information for the Louvre museum for the next 3 months and then tell me about the best Italian and Chinese restaurants in the area of Paris?"

function.name: restaurant_info
function.description: Get restaurant information for a specific area. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: Location for which to find restaurants.

food_type.description: Type of cuisine for which to find restaurants. Default is 'all' if not specified.

function.name: exhibition_info
function.description: Get exhibition information for a specific museum. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

museum_name.description: Name of the museum for which to find exhibitions.

month.description: Number of upcoming months for which to retrieve exhibition details. Default is 1 if not specified.

message.reasoning:
The user wants two pieces of info:

1) Exhibition info for Louvre museum for next 3 months.

2) Best Italian & Chinese restaurants in Paris (area unspecified; maybe general). The tool requires location param as string. We can use "Paris". Food type optional but we need both types separately? They want best Italian and Chinese restaurants. So call twice or one call each specifying food_type accordingly. But they ask "best Italian and Chinese restaurants in the area of Paris." Could interpret as get top restaurants for those cuisines within Paris. We'll do separate calls: first for Italian, second for Chinese. Provide results sorted by rating descending. Use limit=5. For exhibition, month=3. Then produce output JSON array containing objects with keys: name, description, start_date, end_date, image_url, rating, address, phone_number, website, opening_hours, menu_link, price_range, reservation_required, dietary_options, recommended_dishes, average_rating, reviews_count, distance_from_louvre_km, latitude, longitude. Also include exhibition fields: title, dates, curator, highlights, ticket_price, age_restriction, accessibility_features, special_events, virtual_tour_available, related_exhibitions, gallery_location, exhibit_id. And also include overall rating and review count for museums? Not needed.

We should combine into single response object per request? Actually spec says return an array of objects where each object contains all relevant data from the requested APIs. That means each API result becomes an object. So we will have three objects: one for exhibition, one for Italian restaurants list, one for Chinese restaurants list. Each object includes its own fields plus common ones like rating etc. Let's create structure accordingly.

We'll make calls via function calls.
